title: Acute lower abdominal or pelvic pain
population: Adults, including women of reproductive age
priority: Abdominal pain is the leading ED reason for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Pain in the lower abdomen or pelvis; its location narrows the list.

layer0.label: Pregnancy status
layer0.detail: Urine or serum beta-hCG is the first step in women who could be pregnant.

layer0.label: Exam clues
layer0.detail: Migration from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant suggests appendicitis; left lower quadrant tenderness suggests diverticulitis.

layer0.label: Patient group
layer0.detail: Adult, child or pregnant; this changes which imaging comes first.

gate.label: Positive pregnancy test with pain
gate.detail: Ectopic pregnancy must be considered; ultrasound first.

gate.label: Not pregnant
gate.detail: Choose imaging by suspected source: gynecologic or not.

gate_note: Urgent causes to consider first in women of reproductive age include ectopic pregnancy, ruptured ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, appendicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease.

hypotheses.name: Appendicitis
hypotheses.clue: Pain migrating to the right lower quadrant

hypotheses.name: Ovarian cyst or pelvic inflammatory disease
Ureteral stone
hypotheses.clue: Flank pain radiating; see flank pain

steps.title: History and exam
steps.description: Location and migration of pain narrow the list.

appy.text: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant.

torsion.text: Right- or left-sided pelvic pain keeps torsion on the list.

stone.text: Right-sided pelvic pain can also be a stone.

steps.title: Pregnancy test
steps.timing: Before imaging, in anyone who could be pregnant
steps.description: Decides whether pregnancy causes are possible and which imaging is safe.

ectopic.text: A negative serum beta-hCG essentially excludes acute ectopic pregnancy.

steps.title: Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler
steps.description: Transabdominal plus transvaginal ultrasound is the usual first imaging.

ectopic.text: First-line imaging when hCG is positive.

torsion.text: Ultrasound with Doppler is the initial study for gynecologic causes.

gyn.text: Characterizes cysts and complications of pelvic inflammatory disease.

appy.text: First choice in children and pregnancy; often inconclusive in pregnancy, then MRI.

steps.title: Contrast CT
steps.timing: Nonpregnant adults with a suspected non-gynecologic cause
steps.description: Most accurate test for appendicitis and other bowel causes.

appy.text: CT is the most accurate study for appendicitis and its alternatives.

divert.text: CT with IV contrast is best for gastrointestinal causes such as diverticulitis.

evidence.text: Cochrane review: at 43% prevalence, a positive CT means about a 92% chance of appendicitis and a negative CT about 4%.

appy.validation: ACR criteria for test choice; Cochrane diagnostic review for accuracy.

eliminate_when.text: Negative CT in an adult: at a 43% prevalence the probability of appendicitis falls to about 4% (Cochrane review). A strong reduction, not certainty.

do_not_rely.text: A single inconclusive ultrasound in pregnancy; most are inconclusive, so MRI follows.

torsion.no_rule_note: No explicit exclusion rule extracted; ultrasound with Doppler is the first study.

stone.no_rule_note: Route lives in the flank pain situation.

gaps.title: Upper abdominal pain
gaps.text: Right upper quadrant and epigastric pain are not covered; ultrasound is the usual first test for right upper quadrant pain.

gaps.title: Operator dependence
gaps.text: Ultrasound performance depends on operator training.

gaps.title: Clinical scores
gaps.text: Scores such as Alvarado were not sourced in this pass.
